notes: Profile: mid-market analytics SaaS; product-led growth; shipping contextual in-app assistant + semantic search
Primary drivers: latency consistency for chat, lower per‑token cost at scale, predictable throughput during feature launches
Current stack: AWS (us-east-1 primary), Postgres, internal event pipeline; will require VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated
Evaluation summary: started with Hosted API to prove integration speed; metrics looked good for prototyping but peaky traffic during releases drove cost concerns
POC ask: Dedicated environment with reserved GPU capacity for 3 weeks; run canary with 10% traffic -> 50% -> full; measure latency, error rate, and cost per token
Canary plan details discussed on call:
- Step 0: Smoke test on internal test harness in staging VPC
- Step 1 (canary-10): Route 10% traffic to Dedicated pool using weight-based routing; run for 48h; collect p50/p95 latency and token cost
- Step 2 (canary-50): If canary-10 SLOs met and no regressions in quality, increase to 50% for 24-72h
- Step 3 (full ramp): Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 days with automated rollback triggers
Fallback & routing policies prescribed:
- Model variant fallback: primary model is redwood-gpt-large-8b-quant; fallback to redwood-gpt-medium-4b-quant for failures or when latency spikes > 2x SLO
- Region failover: primary us-east-1 dedicated pool; auto-failover to eu-west-1 read-replica pool for multi-region outage; traffic shift limited to low-latency-compatible routes
- Automatic rollback criteria: sustained p95 > 2x target for 30 minutes OR quality regression on eval prompt set (ROUGE/BLEU drop > configured threshold), or error rate > 1%
POC success metrics (customer):
- Chat p95 <= 250ms for single-turn short prompts (90th percentile during regular traffic),
- Token cost reduction >= 30% vs hosted baseline at forecasted volumes
- No more than 0.5% invocations requiring immediate manual rollback during canary,
- Function-calling correctness on out-of-scope detection above 98% on sample prompts
Security notes: require SSO (SAML) SSO + JIT provisioning; KMS integration for key wrapping; 1 year of audit logs retained in account; CI/CD access controls for model rollouts
Integration notes: product engineers prefer the SDKs (node + python) and want example repo for canary routing logic; asked for a short cookbook for route rules and weights
Pricing: preliminary Dedicated quote provided (PDF in Drive). Finance wants a line-item breakdown by reserved GPU hours, burst capacity, and multi-region standby cost
Quotes from stakeholders: 'We need deterministic latency around launches — if the inference layer is the wildcard, the whole release schedule slips' — VP Product
Operational concerns captured: healthcheck frequency, KV cache warmup plan for model variants, and metrics piping into DataDog (customer uses DataDog) — Redwood to provide tracing hooks
